title: Veterans' Care Quality Transparency Act
official_summary:
Veterans' Care Quality Transparency Act

This bill requires the Government Accountability Office to report on all memoranda of understanding and memoranda of agreement entered into by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) with non-VA entities relating to suicide prevention and the provision or coordination of mental health services.

summary.headline: This law requires the Government Accountability Office to report on VA agreements with outside groups about suicide prevention and mental health care.
summary.what_it_does: The Government Accountability Office, which is Congress's audit agency, must review and report on written agreements the Department of Veterans Affairs has signed with non-VA organizations. The agreements cover suicide prevention and providing or coordinating mental health services. The summary describes a reporting requirement and does not change how these agreements work.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who use VA mental health or suicide prevention services
who_it_affects.how: The law adds a government review of the outside partnerships that may help deliver their care, but it does not change their benefits or eligibility.
The department must make its agreements with non-VA entities on these topics available for the Government Accountability Office to report on.

who_it_affects.group: Non-VA organizations that sign agreements with the VA on mental health or suicide prevention
who_it_affects.how: Their agreements with the VA on these topics may be included in the government report.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on October 20, 2020. The summary does not give a due date for the Government Accountability Office report.
